Marissa / team — quick read: MSA already has an "Order Sequencing" clause but it's somewhat silent on multi-stage committed increases. We can do sequencing without changing termination mechanics, but we should: 
1) Add a short Exhibit A addendum that enumerates the ramp schedule and ties committed tokens to each phase.
2) Clarify billing basis during ramp — prefer per-phase committed buckets with overflow billed at published overage rates (and a floor so we don't lose minimum commitment economics).
3) Include a "Capacity Adjustment Notice" (template) with a 30-day lead time for the first uplift and 60 days for subsequent increases to allow Ops scheduling.

I attached a starter redline: MSA_redlines_vK_20270617.docx (high level; legal can tidy). Two open questions:
- Will Nebula expect retroactive credits if their traffic spikes earlier than the scheduled phase? (my recommendation: no credits; instead allow short-term burst credits only if we agree SLA/latency impact).
- If price tiers change materially after we release a new rate card, decide whether the uplift is priced at signing rates or at the then-current rate. Recommend lock on signing for committed blocks.

If everyone agrees, I can hand the redline to Legal for final language and produce the Exhibit A template.

-Karthik
